items.title: Chico Freeman interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001
items.q: He took me back to Willie “The Lion” Smith and James P. Johnson and Louis Armstrong. I used to have to transcribe their solos.

ctx.x: And did you like that kind of freedom in your music?

Yes I did. I mean it was a new thing for me. I mean I had been playing a lot of straight ahead and pretty mainstream I guess, along with a lot of the R&B stuff and things like that. When I met him he showed me new ways of doing things which was quite startling. Actually it sort of got to me because his way of teaching was — as modern as he was, as he is — his way of teaching was always to go back in history. From him I learned more about the history of jazz than anything else. He took me back to Willie “The Lion”…

history you’re bound to repeat it, and if you want to do things different you’ve got to first know the rules to break them, and all of that. So that was his premise that he operated from. And so it was a great experience for me.
